$comment: AuthaGraph constants from Narukawa 2022, 'Formulation of AuthaGraph Map Projection and an Evaluation of its Distortion', Map (J. Japan Cartographers Association) 60(1):1-16, DOI 10.11212/jjca.60.1_1 (J-STAGE free PDF). The 2022 paper redefines the original curved tetrahedron as 4 congruent cones (<4% radial deviation, TS20:TS2 ~ 1:1.03923) so closed-form equations exist. Working reference implementation: mapshaper '+proj=narukawa2022' (MPL-2.0).
name: AuthaGraph (Narukawa 2022 published formulation)
author: Hajime Narukawa
honesty: Narukawa's 2022 mathematical formulation of the AuthaGraph technique. The commercial map was built by hand in 3D-modeling software; the cone re-definition deviates <4% radially from the original curved tetrahedron. Equal-area only at the level of the 96 regions (triangle NPO at arbitrary P), not infinitesimally — the design is deliberately multi-objective (area, angle, distance balanced).

tetrahedron.comment: Regular tetrahedron vertices on the sphere; pairwise unit-vector dot products = -1/3 (verified). Chosen so coastlines are uncut in the rectangular frame.

vertices.ocean: Arctic — East Siberian Sea (near, but not at, the North Pole)

construction.postProjection: orthographic cone → tetrahedron face, with area-ratio correction

forwardEquations.comment: 1/24-region local coordinates: colatitude rho from vertex N, relative longitude lambda in (0, pi/3). Mirror/rotate for the other 23 regions.
forwardEquations.note: Combined formulas reconstructed per paper eqs 2.22/2.23 and verified numerically against the mapshaper implementation, which matches the paper up to a uniform scale factor of 3/sqrt(2).

publishedDistortion.comment: Paper §3, 312 sample points; Tissot indicatrix derived analytically (eqs 3.7–3.26).
publishedDistortion.comparison: Worse in mean than Lambert equal-area cylindrical (0 / 0.55 rad / 0.57), but distributed to four oceanic tetrahedron vertices instead of concentrating at the poles.
